title: Quantifying Microorganisms at Low Concentrations Using Digital Holographic Microscopy (DHM)
protocol: Prepare sterile LB medium.
Autoclave the LB medium (121 °C, 20 min).
Pour sterilized LB medium into plates containing 15 g agar per liter to make LB-agar plates.
Incubate the "Master" culture medium from a fresh bacterial colony on a shaker at 30 °C for ~12 h.
Harvest Shewanella strains after incubation for 12 hours.
Harvest Serratia after incubation for 8 hours.
Take a spectrophotometric reading (OD600) of the bacterial Master culture, which is expected to be in the range of 0.6 to 0.7.
Subculture 100 µL into 5 mL of medium if the OD600 is not within the desired range and allow cell growth to reach mid-log phase.
Count cells directly using a Petroff-Hausser counting chamber from the Master culture.
Extract a 10 µL sample of the undiluted culture with a micropipette and transfer into the chamber.
Image under a high-dry objective microscope (40X or 63X, NA 0.7 - 0.8) using phase contrast.
Count bacteria in at least 20 squares and average to calculate concentration as the average of 20 squares x dilution factor.
Make serial dilutions of the culture for counting of colony-forming units (CFU).
Transfer 20 µL of the bacterial solution and dilute it with 180 µL saline.
Repeat dilutions until the lowest concentration is ~103 cells/mL.
Take 100 µL from at least two dilutions and plate on an appropriate solid media plate.
Spread with a sterile spreader.
Perform at least 3 replicates of each dilution.
Incubate at an appropriate temperature overnight or until colonies grow.
Count colonies and calculate colony forming units (CFU) according to (# of colonies x dilution factor)/volume plated = CFU/mL.
Average CFU over the replicates.
Make serial dilutions of the Master culture for DHM and post-DHM counting on LB media plates.
Dilute the bacteria into 10 - 15 mL of a minimal medium that will encourage motility but inhibit cell division.
Use 0.9% saline or a more specific motility medium as appropriate.
For Escherichia coli, ensure the medium contains EDTA.
Pull in about 10 mL of the dilution of interest using a sterile syringe.
Connect the syringe to the DHM sample chamber using sterile fittings and tubing.
Sterilize all components of the sample chamber by autoclaving.
Flow the sample from the syringe through the sample chamber continuously using a syringe pump.
Acquire holograms consecutively at an appropriate frame rate.
Create a time-stamp file to log the time of each image capture.
Obtain all holograms at ambient temperature (23°C).
Record holograms by executing a pre-written C++ executable file provided by the camera manufacturer.
Allow sufficient time for the entire 10 mL of sample to be flowed through the DHM.
Inoculate enriched media plates with 100 µL of spent media post-DHM image capture.
Spread inoculated media using a sterile spreader and incubate at appropriate temperature for 24 hours.
Count colonies present on enriched media plates after 24 hours incubation.
Convert hologram videos to 32-bit images in ImageJ (Image-Type-32 bit).
Calculate the median pixel value of the time series of holograms (Image-Stack-Zproject-Median).
Subtract the median value from each respective pixel to eliminate stationary artifacts in the hologram (Process-ImageCalculator-Subtract).
Count the number of visible Airy rings and in-focus cells manually with Point tool.
Use the time-stamp file to calculate the total amount of sample pumped at the time the image was captured.
Calculate cell density by dividing the total number of cells detected by the total volume of sample imaged.
Average 5 - 10 frames for accurate statistics.
Choose representative videos with 10 - 200 cells per frame.
Load raw holograms into reconstruction software.
Draw a Fourier mask in ImageJ to choose the real or virtual image and eliminate sinusoidal noise features.
Reconstruct amplitude and phase at appropriate z-steps by entering the reconstruction distance.
Median subtract the amplitude data to reduce noise as in step 4.1.1.
Plot data as a 3D cube or projection using Volume Viewer plugin.
